disease_label_per_paper: Acute liver failure due to Wilson disease with rescue plasma exchange
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 32-year-old woman presented with jaundice, nausea, bilious vomiting, unrecorded fever, fatigue, somnolence, and one episode of black stool.

She had no previous liver disease, recent travel, heavy alcohol use, IV drug use, new medication, herbal medication, or relevant family history; she had uncomplicated vaginal delivery 7 months earlier.

Exam showed hemodynamic stability, significant right upper quadrant tenderness, liver span 14 cm with hepatomegaly 4 cm below the right costal margin, abdominal distension with flank dullness, and jaundice.

Admission labs showed hemoglobin 3.9 g/dL, WBC 18.4 x10^9/L, platelets 198 x10^9/L, total bilirubin 270 umol/L, ALP <24 U/L, AST 144 U/L, ALT 22 U/L, albumin 27.5 g/L, INR 3.0, BUN 31.4 mg/dL, sodium 136 mEq/L, MELD 31, LDH 776 U/L, reticulocytes 12.9%, fibrinogen 251 mg/dL, ceruloplasmin 0.19 g/L, serum copper 138 ug/dL, and urine copper 12943 ug/24 h.

Transplant transfer was sought but unavailable during COVID-era travel restrictions; she received transfusion, folate, vitamin K, NAC, plasmapheresis on days 3 and 5, penicillamine, pyridoxine, ursodeoxycholic acid, and improved without transplant.
